items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: The cat I was working with was Buster Bennett and Robert Montgomery, just the three of us -- saxophone, bass and piano.

ctx.x: He wasn't with them. It was Thornel. Farnell.

We played a TV show and what made me feel so good, Nat Cole was in town and he didn't play, but he was a guest, you know, and this guy was questioning him. We played out two or three tunes and I had played opposite Nat Cole back in '53, down at the old Blue Note. It was called Lips Low Level then in Chicago. Nat had Charles Norris on bass, John Collins, guitar and Lee Young on drums and himself on piano. We played our set and Nat (unintelligible) would bring his group. I noticed he used to come out and watch us.…

Buster was playing sock cymbal to give us a little leverage, you know, and it seemed like Nat marveled at that. I spoke to him just once -- and like I say, I didn't know of him -- but he remembered me in Philly here in '61 because when we finished the show, they had featured me on the last tune, and I had a little thing I did on Lester Young's "Lester Leaps In," and my solo work, you know. So when I finished, and we were standing there, Nat got up from the dais where he was sitting and started toward the band. So…
